question: Intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) given within 10 days of fever onset in Kawasaki disease significantly reduces the risk of coronary artery aneurysm formation.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is a core fact about Kawasaki management. IVIG 2 g/kg within 10 days of fever onset is the cornerstone of treatment. Without timely IVIG, the risk of coronary artery aneurysm is 20-25%; with it, the risk falls to under 5%.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. IVIG 2 g/kg as a single infusion within 10 days of fever onset reduces the risk of coronary aneurysms from approximately 20-25% to less than 5%. This 10-day window is absolute — missing it substantially increases the risk of the most feared complication.
